records.claimLabel: custodian: software token on the MX95 board (board-local, phase 1; no KMIP); data owner on the Mac; FHE server on the KV260 (untrusted compute)
records.notes: Custodian: the MX95 board (6x Cortex-A55, 8 GB, glibc 2.43) ran the token from a clean aarch64 release build of pqctoday-hsm a0a60b69 (sha256 0d7f4d82…e749); the appliance's own services were untouched. Token setup took 1 s; the export took about 5 s, including the 30,147,061 B compressed server key, the 33,034 B compact public key and two ML-DSA-65 signatures. The KV260 checked the pinned signer, key identity, parameter hash, SHA-384 and signature in 298 ms and refused 3 of 3 bad keys. 7 of 7 results reached the token: 6 released correctly, FheUint64 refused by policy, about 0.45 s each including SSH. The owner reached the MX95 board over the owner's management network over SSH (phase-1 exception; crypto-network-only remains the rule) and the KV260 over the compute board's own network over SSH; the two boards never talked to each other. The signer pin was taken from the export, fetched over the owner's own session; the token's signer attestation was not checked. An earlier attempt the same day is not evidence: a script fault let only 1 of 7 results reach the token; it was fixed in 77d3b29 and the whole flow repeated with a fresh token. The MX95 token's memory was not measured. The run summary is withheld because it names internal hosts; its facts are given here. Journal files are published redacted: the board's host name is replaced by "kv260-board", byte for byte otherwise. Original: journal.txt (original sha256 10f403ec1635cf77341cbea9e138b567136b83e300b8d875daa97ab344cd5e57).

records.notes: PQCTODAY EDUCATIONAL TEST ONLY, on the pre-ceremony-ABI bridge; software tokens on the boards, not hardware custody. Engine pqctoday-hsm a0a60b69; board tool, courier and KMIP test bridge pqctoday-hsm c176fffb (repl_edu_board sha256 110626ae...60f1). Before the run, both boards were bootstrapped under one test root with an FHE-constrained replication policy; the MX95 generated the FHE seed and exported, and the seed was backed up to the MX95 Pro with the offline-backup ceremony over KMIP on the crypto network (TLS 1.3 X25519MLKEM768; 4 s window; receipt host-verified; 6 of 6 negative checks refused). The Pro re-derived its own public material with its own signer. Run: the KV260 checked the server key against both pinned signers in 296 ms and refused 3 of 3 bad keys; the MX95 custodian decided 7 of 7 results (6 released correctly, FheUint64 refused by policy), and the MX95 Pro backup made the same 7 decisions on the same ciphertexts. Medians: u8 add 1.46 s, mul 3.77 s; u32 add 6.00 s; u64 add 12.78 s; cgroup peak 203.1M. Not shown: destroying the seed on the custodian before the backup decrypts, the owner-side signer attestation check, hardware custody. Not covered: direct network access to the service port, concurrent clients, a Yocto service unit.

records.claimLabel: custodian: software token on Mac, signer pinned from a verified attestation; data owner on the Mac; FHE server on the KV260 (untrusted compute)
records.notes: Same flow as the reproduced Mac-token custody run, with one change: before anything is sent to the compute board, the data owner verifies the custodian's key attestation on the fetched export (pqctoday-hsm b3a6eb8d verify-signer, macOS binary sha256 92759d01...f574) and pins the signer only from a passing result. Checked: strict DER evidence with one ML-DSA-65 signature; the chain key-attestation certificate, device and manufacturing root; current CRLs for both issuers; a nonce bound to this export (first 32 bytes of SHA-384 of the server-key manifest); the attested key equals the export's signer key and is sensitive, never extractable and generated in the token; key identity and parameter hash match the manifests. Refused, each with a reason: a manifest with one bit flipped, a replaced signer key, a missing device CRL, a time after the CRLs expire. Then: the KV260 refused 3 of 3 bad server keys; the token decided 7 of 7 results (6 released correctly, FheUint64 refused); cgroup peak 203.1M. Software token on a Mac, not hardware custody. Journal files are published redacted: the board's host name is replaced by "kv260-board", byte for byte otherwise. Original: journal.txt (original sha256 b38773d1871463d076baae39a027aec7418ededb4033fb0fe74a03a720b64d26).

records.claimLabel: custodian: software token on a Mac; untrusted compute: the KV260 FHE service installed in the shipped board image, over mutual TLS; owner verified the attestation
records.notes: PQCTODAY EDUCATIONAL TEST ONLY; software token on a Mac, not hardware custody. First run of the FHE service installed in the shipped KV260 image (CACP K26 build 20261004145201, see IMAGE-PROVENANCE.md), not a binary copied to /tmp: the three pins were written to /run/pqc/fhe-server.env and the baked systemd unit pqc-fhe-server was started; without pins the unit does not start (its start condition checks for the pin file, see installed-unit.txt). The client ran in a linux/arm64 container on the owner's Mac (pqctoday-fhe cd2271ce) and connected straight to the board's crypto port 5730 over mutual TLS. The owner checked the token's attestation with the macOS build of pqctoday-hsm b3a6eb8d verify-signer (against the token's own test root; signer 891ce509...) and pinned the signer. A tampered server key was refused (403); the signed server key was admitted (verify 235 ms, conformant load and decompress 1.50 s). A 7-step program over u32, u8 and u64 ran in 48.6 s on the board (list expansion 14.3 s, steps 34.3 s; 50.2 s wall at the client). That is slower than the 42.7 s of the 3 Oct service run: the installed unit restricts the service to CPUs 1-3, while the earlier run used all four cores, which is the likely reason but was not isolated. The token released 5 of 6 outputs, all correct, and refused the u64 output by policy (CK_RV 0x1b). cgroup peak 265 MiB against a 3 GiB limit. The service pins live in memory only and are lost on reboot; the board image has no ss command, so one line in installed-unit.txt is an error message. The board's journal is withheld because it names the board.
